html:
A huge artificial harbour at the mouth of the Tiber, begun by the emperor Claudius and enlarged by Trajan. For about five hundred years it was the main port of ancient Rome.

Rome needed vast amounts of imported grain, much of it from Egypt (see Egypt feeds Rome). The old river port of Ostia had no safe harbour for big ships, so they unloaded far to the south at Puteoli. Claudius built a basin a few kilometres north of Ostia, with two long moles running into the sea. A lighthouse stood on an island made by sinking a giant ship, the one Caligula had used to bring an obelisk from Egypt, filled with concrete.

The basin was still too open. Tacitus says a storm in 62 CE sank some two hundred ships inside it. Around 112 CE Trajan dug a sheltered inner basin with six sides, ringed by warehouses, and linked it by canal to the Tiber. Goods came in from across the empire, among them the grain for the Roman grain dole.

The harbour later silted up. Its hexagonal basin survives inland, near Rome's Fiumicino airport.
sum: A huge artificial harbour at the mouth of the Tiber, begun by the emperor Claudius and enlarged by Trajan. For about five hundred years it was the main port of ancient Rome.
